question: A mob of seven villagers armed with sticks and axes enters an disputed agricultural field to forcibly harvest crops belonging to their neighbor, threatening to kill anyone who intervenes. Analyze this collective action under the Pakistan Penal Code: state the specific offence, cite the section defining the assembly, and cite the section prescribing the punishment.
answer: This collective action constitutes the offence of being a member of an unlawful assembly under the Pakistan Penal Code. Section 141 PPC defines an unlawful assembly as an assembly of five or more persons whose common object is to enforce any right or supposed right by means of criminal force. Section 143 PPC prescribes the punishment, providing that whoever is a member of an unlawful assembly shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine, or with both. [PPC Section 141] [PPC Section 143]

question: A Provincial Government files a constitutional writ petition before a Provincial High Court challenging a decision of the Federal Government regarding natural resource royalties. Can the High Court exercise jurisdiction under Article 199 of the Constitution of Pakistan in light of Article 175E? Synthesize both provisions.
answer: No, the High Court cannot exercise jurisdiction. Under Article 199 of the Constitution, the High Court writ jurisdiction is subject to the Constitution and conditional on no other adequate remedy being provided by law. Under Article 175E(1) of the Constitution (inserted by the 27th Amendment Act, 2025), the Federal Constitutional Court has original jurisdiction to the exclusion of every other court in any dispute between two or more Governments (defined as the Federal Government and Provincial Governments). Because Article 175E explicitly excludes all other courts in inter-governmental disputes, the High Court Article 199 jurisdiction is constitutionally ousted in favor of the exclusive original jurisdiction of the Federal Constitutional Court. [Constitution Article 199] [Constitution Article 175E]

Analyzes Article 175E(1) granting exclusive original jurisdiction to the Federal Constitutional Court in inter-governmental disputes.
Concludes that Article 175E ousts the High Court Article 199 writ jurisdiction in disputes between the Federal Government and a Provincial Government.

question: How do Articles 175A, 175B, and 175C of the Constitution of Pakistan conjointly govern the establishment, judicial strength, and appointment of Judges to the Federal Constitutional Court? Synthesize these provisions.
answer: Under Article 175B, the Federal Constitutional Court is established consisting of a Chief Justice and as many other Judges as determined by Act of Parliament or fixed by the President. Under Article 175C(1), the Chief Justice and each Judge of the Federal Constitutional Court are appointed by the President in accordance with the procedure laid down in Article 175A. Under Article 175A, nominations are initiated and processed through the Judicial Commission of Pakistan before appointment. Together, these three provisions establish the court (Art. 175B), require presidential appointment under constitutional procedure (Art. 175C), and mandate nomination via the Judicial Commission (Art. 175A). [Constitution Article 175A] [Constitution Article 175B] [Constitution Article 175C]

question: Which offences under PECA 2016 are explicitly classified as cognizable and non-bailable under Section 43, in exception to the general rule that PECA offences are non-cognizable and bailable?
answer:
Under Section 43 of PECA 2016, the general rule is that all offences under the Act, and abetment thereof, are non-cognizable, bailable and compoundable (Section 43(1)), subject to specific statutory exceptions:
1. Under Section 43(2), offences under sections 10 (Cyber terrorism), 13 (Electronic forgery), 14 (Electronic fraud), 20 (Offences against dignity), 21 (Offences against modesty), 22 (Child pornography), 22A (Online grooming), 22B (Commercial sexual exploitation of children), 22C (Use of information system for kidnapping/trafficking of minor) and 26A (Punishment for false and fake information), as well as abetment thereof, are explicitly non-bailable, non-compoundable and cognizable by the investigation agency.
2. Under the Proviso to Section 43(1), offences under section 17 (Unauthorized issuance of SIM cards) are cognizable by the investigation agency on a written complaint by the Authority (Pakistan Telecommunication Authority). [PECA Section 43]

expected_citations.title: Offences to be compoundable and non-cognizable
